doc.title: Candido Camero — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Montparnasse, Jovenes Sociales, Apolo and Bolero del 35
summary: He lists successive groups and instruments (Montparnasse on bass, Jovenes Sociales on guitar, Apolo on tres, then Tata Gutierrez's Bolero) and the members of Septeto Apolo.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Name the other contemporary groups of that time.
From that time?
Youth groups of that age.

From that time, there was Gloria Habanera. Then there was, the group, the Septeto Montparnasse. I don’t remember the musicians well, the names, because well you know so many years, but I remember the Montparnasse as it was called. After the Gloria Habanera I worked with the Montparnasse.
How long were you with them?
In Montparnasse, about . . . about five years.
And what instrument did you play?

There I played the bass. Later there was another conjunto, septet from, the town of Regla - a septet called Jovenes Sociales. They were from Regla. The director's name was Jose Salinas. We called him Cheo. There I played guitar.
The tres.
No, the guitar.
Ah, the guitar.
Yes, the guitar. After Los Jovenes Sociales, El Apolo.
How long were you with the Apolo?
With Apolo, I was there about five years.
And what instrument did you play?
I played the tres there. After the Apolo, I was with the Bolero del ’35 de Tata Gutierrez, where I also played tres. The bongo player in that group was Mongo Santamaria. And then the orchestra . . .
Let’s return to the Apolo Septet. Apart from Mongo, who else was part of the group?

Well, starting with Mongo on bongos, Bebo Alan on bass, Miguel Luis, no Jose Luis on claves - sorry, Modesto Perez on claves, later he was the singer in the Hermanos Contreras Orchestra. Let's put them in order again. Mongo Santamaria on bongos, Bebo Alan on bass, Modesto Perez on the claves, Miguel Luís on maracas, and Raul Diaz who was the director on the guitar. And the other, the other trumpet was, Miguelito, Miguelito, Miguelito, I am trying to remember the name now, Miguelito, well now I do not remember the last name of the trumpeter. Miguelito . . . Moliné – Miguelito Moliné was the trumpeter.
Now maestro, what year are we talking about more or less?
Excuse me?
What year are we talking about?

Well, I was twenty two years old at that time. Yes I was twenty two years old. That was long before my first child was born and now he is an adult. He has a wife, has grandchildren, great grandchildren, and I have also grandchildren and great grandchildren. Yes, I was about twenty two years old when I was in that group. I do not remember the year exactly. I think it was like in ‘40, not ‘40, ‘40 something, ‘40. A very good conjunto. A very good septet.
